content.overview: A mock recall tests whether records can rapidly identify source, downstream scope, location and accountable contacts. It is an exercise in system capability, not proof of legal compliance for every jurisdiction.

vocabulary.definition: Controlled exercise used to test traceability and response capability without representing a real market action.
Reconciliation of quantities received, transformed, lost, held and distributed.
Verification that intended contacts, controls or recoveries were achieved.

sections.title: Start with a defined trigger and scope hypothesis
sections.body: The exercise should identify the event, starting record and assumptions while allowing evidence to expand or narrow scope.

sections.title: Trace in both directions
sections.body: Source history and all downstream children, samples, packages and destinations should be identified using event records.

sections.title: Reconcile and document gaps
sections.body: Quantities, locations, response times, contacts and missing records should be measured and assigned corrective action.

workedExamples: A package-lot trigger traces back to two parent lots and forward to retained, held and distributed units; quantities are reconciled rather than inferred.
commonMistakes: Tracing only to the immediate parent.
Calling an exercise successful despite unexplained gaps.
content.practicalApplication: Run a paper mock recall and record trace-back, trace-forward, mass balance, response time, gaps and improvement actions.
content.summary: Mock recall performance is demonstrated by complete, timely, reconciled and improvable traceability evidence.
